title: INDIAN NAVY–US NAVY EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE DISPOSAL EXERCISE 2026 TO COMMENCE AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI
body_text:
The Indian Navy–US Navy Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Exercise 2026 is scheduled to be conducted at Southern Naval Command, Kochi, from 10 to 14 Aug 2026 . The bilateral exercise aims to enhance interoperability and strengthen professional cooperation between the specialist diving and EOD teams of the two navies.
The five-day exercise will comprise Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-training, equipment demonstrations and scenario-based practical exercises . The programme will facilitate the exchange of contemporary EOD methodologies, emerging technologies and Best Practices , while providing both sides an opportunity to gain insights into each other’s capabilities, operational concepts and employment philosophies.
The exercise is designed to promote collaborative learning and operational synergy, enabling personnel from both navies to refine procedures, enhance mutual understanding and strengthen their ability to respond effectively to complex and evolving EOD challenges.
The Indian Navy and US Navy have been conducting joint Salvage and EOD exercises since 2005 . The forthcoming engagement marks the eighth edition of this specialised bilateral training exercise and underscores the enduring commitment of the two navies towards enhancing interoperability, sharing operational expertise and strengthening cooperation in specialised maritime operations.

enrichment.summary: The Indian Navy and US Navy will conduct the eighth edition of their bilateral Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Exercise from 10-14 August 2026 at Southern Naval Command, Kochi. The five-day exercise involves Subject Matter Expert Exchanges, cross-training, equipment demonstrations and scenario-based drills aimed at enhancing interoperability between the specialist diving and EOD teams of both navies. The two navies have conducted joint Salvage and EOD exercises since 2005.
enrichment.context: India-US defence cooperation has deepened significantly over the past two decades, moving from occasional engagements to a comprehensive strategic partnership encompassing joint exercises across all three services, defence trade, technology sharing (like iCET), and logistics agreements (LEMOA, COMCASA, BECA). The EOD/Salvage exercise series, running since 2005, is one of the longer-standing bilateral naval engagements and reflects sustained cooperation in specialized maritime security domains, distinct from larger exercises like MALABAR. EOD and diving cooperation is significant because it deals with mine countermeasures, underwater ordnance disposal, and port/harbour security capabilities that are critical for safeguarding sea lanes of communication and coastal infrastructure. Southern Naval Command in Kochi is a key training and operational hub of the Indian Navy, hosting premier institutions like the Naval Base and various training establishments. Such exercises also fit into the broader Indo-Pacific strategic framework, where India and the US collaborate to ensure a free, open, and secure maritime domain, particularly relevant given increasing focus on undersea security, maritime domain awareness, and countering non-traditional threats like sea mines and improvised explosive devices in coastal waters.
